analysis:
All four units are test-only changes: DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift (modified; fixture(artifact:) parameter, served-history build gating tests, Qwen assistant selection/public-traffic tests, onLargeStack helper) and a new EngineV2ResliceFloorWiringTests.swift (re-slice floor orchestration using stub engines, with no network, keys or real weights). No production source is changed in the supplied units, so no new attack surface, trust-boundary change or control weakening is introduced.

Security-relevant behavior the tests assert, which is encouraging for the threat model:
- Served speed records from other worker builds, concurrent requests or foreign ranks are excluded from calibration (lines ~401-436).
- A saved config's tensorAssistant policy is strictly decoded, with duplicate keys, extra fields, type confusion and a dropped policy rejected (lines ~1025-1079).
- Assistant-decoded plans are not advertised as public-traffic qualified (lines ~935-970).
- Saved pipeline-mode records are refused for start and save (lines ~655-697).
- Index and link-probe history files are written 0600 (lines ~494, 579).
- KV re-slice preserves per-slot floors and refuses infeasible admission (new file).

The test helper at lines ~466-475 writes a 0700 shell script in a temp home, which is test-only. The patch excerpt for the test-file head was truncated, but the full head text was supplied for lines 393-1116.

Remaining question for integration: the production code behind these tests (ClusterSetupPlanning, ClusterPairOwnerServing, EngineV2KVSizing, StandaloneServer and ProviderLoop reslice) is not in the supplied units, so I cannot confirm that the production behavior matches the asserted contracts. No finding is raised. T-041 is only tangentially touched, since the tests concern KV grants rather than cache storage.
